1  AWARD DATED 29.11.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.56/2019 ON  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:5004  MFA No. 1164 of 2021 THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT.XI, TUMAKURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION. 
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 29.11.2019 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.XI, Tumakuru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.56/2019. This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation. Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal. 
3. Brief facts of the case are as under;
The claimant was traveling as a passenger in private bus bearing registration No.KA-06-D-3434 on 08.11.2018 at about 3.45 p.m. from Huliyar to Sira town on NH-4 road. The driver of the said bus drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and NC:
2024:KHC:5004 safety, lost control of the vehicle and he applied sudden brake. Due to the said impact, passengers fell down from the seats and the claimant dashed against the iron rod and sustained fractures. Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sira, wherein, he was admitted as an inpatient for a period of one week. Thereafter, to Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Center, Tumakuru and he was admitted as an inpatient for a period of 10 days and discharged with an advise to follow up treatment. The claimant spent more than Rs.75,000/- towards treatment,
attendant, transport and other expenses. 
3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of accident, aged about 35 years, he was earning an income of Rs.30,000/- per month by doing carpentry work. Due to the occurrence of accident and injuries suffered, the claimant is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of accident. Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation. 
NC: 2024:KHC:5004 3.2 On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and respondent No.1 filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle. Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition. 
Girish @ Mudalagiriyappa vs Anandakumar on 6 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50755120/
2 3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined himself as PW.1, Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P15. On the other hand, respondents did not adduce their evidence, but marked document as Ex.R1, 3.5 On the basis of material evidence,
both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,97,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till deposit. 
NC: 2024:KHC:5004 3.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award. 
4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court. Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation. 
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference. Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal. 
6. Having heard the learned counsel for appellant- claimant and learned counsel for Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award, the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P15, which are police and medical records, which apparently seen that FIR NC:
2024:KHC:5004 and charge sheet laid against the driver of the offending vehicle, which is not disputed by the driver in any criminal proceedings and medical records are produced to prove the injuries sustained and expenditure met by the claimant. However, negligence is rightly attributed as against the driver of the offending vehicle. 
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income, it is stated that age of the claimant was 33 years as on the date of occurrence of accident. The tribunal taken the income of Rs.10,000/- per month, in view of there being no proof of income. However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.12,500/- for the accident year 2018. Accordingly,
income is taken as Rs.12,500/-. The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '16', which does not call for interference. 
8. PW.2-Doctor has assessed the disability at 66% to the both upper limbs and 22% to the whole body, whereas, the tribunal not accepting the version of PW.2- NC: 2024:KHC:5004 Doctor,
adopted the disability at 10% without there being any basis or reasoning. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that unless there is contra material evidence placed on record to dispute the evidence of PW.2-Doctor, the tribunal, in normal circumstances, should not disturb the disability assessed by PW.2-Doctor. Of course, the tribunal is at liberty and discretion to assess the functional disability and physical disability or retained the same as expressed by PW.2- Doctor, unless contra material is placed, which is cogent enough to accept the said version of the Doctor, who is an expert in the field of medicine. Hence, the disability in the present case will have Girish @ Mudalagiriyappa vs Anandakumar on 6 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50755120/
3 to be taken at 22%.
9. Learned counsel for appellant-claimant also contends that future prospects has to be awarded in the present case, considering the fact that the claimant is a carpenter by profession. Since no material is placed on record to show firstly he is a Carpenter and secondly, the disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body, it does NC: 2024:KHC:5004 not warrant interference. Accordingly,
the same is negatived. Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.5,28,000/- (Rs.12,500/- x 12 x 16 x 22%) towards loss of future income as against Rs.1,92,000/-
awarded by the tribunal. 
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.40,000/- towards food and nourishment, which do not call for interference and the same is retained. 
11. Towards medical expenses, Rs.65,065/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which also does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period. In view of this Court enhancing the income from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.12,500/-, the claimant would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day NC: 2024:KHC:5004 activities. Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.50,000/- (Rs.12,500/- x 4) under this head. 
13. The tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses, whereas, PW.2-Doctor has adduced in his evidence that Rs.50,000/- would be required for future medical expenses. I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.10,000/-. In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.30,000/- (Rs.20,000/- + Rs.10,000/-) under this head. 
14. The tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities. I deem it appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- under this head. 
15. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,93,065/- as against Rs.3,97,000/- as mentioned in the table below: 
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 50,000-00 Medical expenses 65,065-00 Food and nourishment 40,000-00  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:5004 Loss of income during laid 50,000-00 up period Loss of future income 5,28,000-00 Girish @ Mudalagiriyappa vs Anandakumar on 6 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50755120/
4 Loss of amenities 30,000-00 Future medical expenses 30,000-00  TOTAL 7,93,065-00 16. Accordingly, I pass the following: 
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed-in-part;
ii) The judgment and award dated 29.09.2019 passed by Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.XI, Tumakuru in MVC.No.56/2019 is modified;
iii) The claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,93,065/- as against Rs.3,97,000/-
iv) The enhanced compensation amount shall be paid by the respondent-Insurance Company with interest @ 6% p.a. within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order; 
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:5004 v) The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the appellant-claimant upon proper verification.

14. The tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities.
I deem it appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 50,000-00
Loss of amenities 30,000-00 Future medical expenses 30,000-00
Accordingly, I pass the following:

ORDER i) The appeal is allowed-in-part;
ii) The judgment and award dated 29.09.2019 passed by Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T.XI, Tumakuru in MVC.No.56/2019 is modified;
iii) The claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,93,065/- as against Rs.3,97,000/-
iv) The enhanced compensation amount shall be paid by the respondent-Insurance Company with interest @ 6% p.a. within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order;
